overview.description: Noms (Nomination Whist / Small Ships Rules) is a 4-player British trick-taking game with secret partnerships. Players bid from 10 upward, and the winner nominates a card to determine their secret partner (revealed when played). history.origins: Noms is a British Royal Navy card game tradition, also known as 'Small Ships Rules.' It represents the naval variant of Nomination Whist, distinct from other games using the same name. The secret partnership mechanic and no-shuffle rule reflect the unique conditions of shipboard play.
timeline: 19th-20th Century: Played aboard Royal Navy vessels
Mid-20th Century: Rules formalized as 'Small Ships Rules'
Present: Preserved by naval veterans and card game enthusiasts
history.evolution: The game developed the secret partnership mechanic to add intrigue to shipboard entertainment. The no-shuffle rule may have originated from limited playing space or superstition.
history.cultural: Strong British naval tradition. The 'Small Ships Rules' name indicates its association with smaller naval vessels where crew size made 4-player games practical.

setup.players: 4 players. Partnerships are secret and determined by card nomination.
setup.dealing: 13 cards each, dealt in packets (4-3 pattern rotating). Cards are NOT shuffled between handsâ€”only cut.

rules.objective: Bidding team: win at least the bid number of tricks. Secret partnership revealed during play when nominated card is played.
rules.gameplay: If all pass, next hand is 'double hand' (stakes doubled). Follow suit if possible. Standard trick-taking rules apply.
keyRules: Cards NOT shuffled between handsâ€”only cut
Winner nominates a card to determine secret partner
All pass = double hand next round

strategy.basic: Bid with strong hands. As declarer, nominate a card you hold (for solo) or that you believe a strong opponent holds (to make them your partner).
strategy.intermediate: The no-shuffle rule means card memory is crucialâ€”track which cards were played in previous hands. Use this knowledge to nominate cards strategically.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing and deduction. As a defender, try to deduce who the secret partner is from the bidding and early play. Coordinate with your unknown partner without explicit communication.
tips: Remember: NO shufflingâ€”card memory is everything
Nominating an Ace or King you don't hold is risky; partner might be weak in that suit
MisÃ¨re is powerful when you have a very weak hand
Watch for tells when the secret partner is revealed

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Highest trump wins trick; if no trump played, highest card of led suit wins.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Highest bidder leads to first trick; thereafter winner of each trick leads.

edgeCases.text: All four pass: next hand is double hand; cards stacked and cut without shuffling.
Mis a Vis: after first trick bidder exposes remaining 12 cards face up.
Nominated card in bidder's hand: bidder plays alone; opponents do not know initially they are all on same team.
Double hand: all scores for that deal are doubled.

customActions.description: Declarer names a card; the holder of that card is the secret partner, revealed when the card is played. Declarer may nominate a card in own hand to play alone.
customActions.constraints: Only in nomination phase after winning the bid.

customActions.description: Declarer announces trump suit or no trumps when leading to the first trick. If no suit stated after a number bid, the suit led is trumps.
customActions.constraints: Only in nomination phase; must state trump or no trumps when leading first trick.

customActions.description: Score the contract: success means bidder and partner each score the bid amount; failure means opponents score the bid. Solo: bidder alone or all three opponents. Mis scores 13, Mis a Vis 26; double hand doubles all scores.
customActions.constraints: Only in scoring phase after all 13 tricks played.
